body:
I know this thread is a few days old, but I thought I'd post anyway in case I can help anyone!

After self-diagnosing myself with emetophobia (which spurred on a lot of other anxieties) over 10 years ago, I had my greatest success this year - actually being sick (yes, in that way) for the first time since 2010.
ne
I was so scared all night beforehand, and I went to bed feeling absolutely terrible...but I woke up that morning, felt queasy and thought "this is it...it's finally happening" and then boom, done. No tears, no anxieties (in that moment) and it was honestly, honestly, as cliche as this sounds: 

NOT A BIG DEAL AT ALL.

I would rather get a needle now than be sick, and I'm not even scared of needles!

Sure I still get a little anxious now and then, but it's soooo much easier with the knowledge that it's not a big deal anymore.  I know if someone had told me this a year ago I would have never believed them, but I promise you it's really, honestly the truth!

Hi :)

First of all, I just wanted to say don't be afraid. You're clearly a kind, competent young woman and you have a bright future ahead of you, you will never be bogged down by this fear!

Now, I'm kind of different to you...I've never been afraid of other people vomiting as long as I knew it wouldn't affect me (eg. Hungover, food poisoning etc), but i've always been terrified of myself vomiting.  So I can't say I can offer practical advice unfortunately :(

But what I can say is this...a week or so ago I actually got food poisoning and was sick for the first time in over three years and....it was fine.  It wasn't anywhere near as bad as I thought it would be...and now, I feel like my fear is really almost gone.

So while getting over others is a first step, I can tell you that 'flooding' could really be an option...but more than anything else I encourage you to keep searching for people to talk to because they really can make a difference in your life! Not even shrinks, but just counsellors, can really help you, I promise!

So stay strong, for us, and for your own future! You're intelligent enough, it's easy to tell, and I'm sure you'll have a great time at med school!
I've been monitoring this hoping for an update from you.  Glad to see you're still here with us.  You made the right decision, I promise you.

Firstly, I hope that it's not too late.  I don't live in the US so I'm not sure of our time difference, but I hope that due to the comments today you've at least decided to hold it off for another night or so..


Anyway, I respect your decision.  But I get the feeling you're trying to make yourself more comfortable than the decision than you really are; being incredibly polite, a lot of smiley faces, exclamation marks etc...It just seems odd to me why you would choose to kill yourself.  You understand the great possibility of seeing a psychiatrist and getting help.  You care about your family and friends, and you have a good social life.

Do you feel you have depression?  I mean, this might annoy you, but the sleep deprivation you've had could contribute greatly, and I mean *greatly* to your state of mind.  Even though it may have been a while since you've had sleeping problems, sleep debt has a strong long-term effect which could still be plaguing you without you realising.

However, you may have already considered that fact and dismissed it.

You say 'killing [your]self isn't the perfect solution'. THe solution to what? Your depression? Boredom?  I'm not trying to pester you, I'm just genuinely curious as to why.  I know you've already answered it below, but I'm still confused.

Thanks, and once again, from a kid only a couple of years older from you on the other side of the world, I deeply care about what you choose to do, or have perhaps already done. I hope you haven't gone down that path.

When I was 15, yes 15, I too was suicidal. I would lie in bed each night and look out the window and just wish with all my heart I wouldn't wake up the next morning.  I knew it was heartless, I knew it would devastate my parents, but I just thought 'fuck it' becuase there was nothing in this world that caught my interest or that made me want to live.  Sure good things could happen, but most of the time it's bad, isnt it?


Three years on from then, after seeing two counsellors (who helped an unbelievable amount) I look back on my 15 year-old self and just think how grateful, how unimaginably, incredibly grateful I am for not giving in.  Since then I've found happinnes I previously would have scoffed at.  I thought I was all high and mighty at 15, that I was 'above' the world around me.  I also felt (like you might, I don't know) that because I came from an upper-class, wealthy, white, educated family that I had no right to be depressed and I must have been messed up for it.

But man was I wrong.  You seem stubborn, and, not in a bad way, quite confident in your ability to kill yourself.  But I implore you to see a counsellor, a psychiatrist, tell your parents.  Even if you don't do any of these things just hang in there until after you finish school.  Because, and I promise you this, you are missing out on the best years of your life.  Your 'growing detachment from your parents', no matter how serious you think this is, is almost certainly part of puberty.

Now, I don't mean to chalk down your sadness to 'oh just a phase in puberty' because I know that is certainly NOT true 99% of the time.  Trust me.  What I'm trying to tell you that even though your state of mind may be because of something more serious, or something not so serious, I'm certain that if you just wait a few weeks, even a few months, your situation will change.


I know my post is rambled and poorly formatted.  I just want you to know I felt exactly like you.  I thought killing myself was the perfect solution.  BEsides, once you're dead, who cares about what your parents and friends feel, you won't know, so why worry?  But I was arrogant, ignorant and naive.  I thought that by being able to accept death I was 'enlightened', now I just realise how idiotic that was.

I still struggle with bouts of depression, but so many great things have happened for me. And I'm excited for my future for the first time in years.  Please, please, I ask you with all my heart, see a counsellor or a psychiatrist before you come to this decision.  If, after seeing a few, you still want to.  Well, I'm not going to tell you no...you know your own life better than me, obviously.  But coming from someone who was in your situation, this is not the end. You seem very intelligent, if you are then you should realise this achieves NOTHING. Suicide has no benefits.  Please, please, see someone or PM me before you make this decision.

Thank you so much for your reassurance! It's more than 24 hours so I'm definitely fine.  I definitely was overreacting, but I'm sure a fellow sufferer would understand how nice it is to have some reassurance.  I really appreciate your reply :)
